_comment: UI redesign, landing 1 of N. See docs/UI_REDESIGN_DESIGN.md SS5 and SS10 item 2. This ticket is the READ half of the host-agnostic core layer: a conformance snapshot the UI renders. It is purely additive -- it must not change a single live write path -- and it is identical whether the UI ends up a browser page or WPF, which is why it goes first. UI2 (the config path made single-owner) and UI3 (the window's disposition) follow and are NOT in scope here.

tickets.title: Copier read model: a conformance snapshot, with measured-vs-unmeasured metrics
tickets.defect: There is no read path that can answer the operator's question -- 'is each follower doing what I configured it to do?' Three concrete gaps, all verified against the file. (1) NO COMPARISON EXISTS. The expected-vs-actual follower position is computed only as a side effect of correcting it, inside ReconcileFollowerPosition, whose delta math at TradeCopierEngine.cs:191-192 sits inside `#if !TESTING` -- so nothing can read the comparison and no test can execute it. Every consumer that wants to know whether the copier is conforming has to recompute the sizing itself, which is a second implementation of the rule and will drift from the first. (2) A ZERO METRIC IS INDISTINGUISHABLE FROM A CLEAN ONE. `rel.LatencyMs` (:58) and `rel.AvgSlippageTicks` (:59) are session-scoped and reset on recompile, and the only UI for them is an interpolated status string at TradeCopierWindow.cs:799 that renders them as bare numbers. So 'no fill has been observed yet' and 'a fill was observed and was perfect' both display as 0. That exact confusion was misdiagnosed as a broken measurement and cost two sessions as `P?-66`; the measurement was never broken. Worse, `LatencyMs` is left at its PREVIOUS value when a reading is rejected by the sanity bound, so a stale number can be displayed as if it were current. (3) SAMPLE COUNTS EXIST FOR ONE METRIC ONLY. `_slippageSampleCounts` (:3342, keyed by `rel.Id`) counts slippage samples so the running mean at :3346 is correct, but there is NO equivalent for latency -- so even a consumer that wanted to distinguish unmeasured from measured cannot do it for the latency figure.
tickets.spec:
Add a pure read API, `TradeCopierEngine.GetSnapshot()`, returning a DTO the UI can render directly. Purely additive: NO live write path may change.

A. ENUMERATION. The snapshot MUST enumerate relationships the same way the engine ACTS on them, not by walking `_relationships` and `_groups` separately. `GetActiveRelationshipsForLeader` already expands groups into relationships AND applies `P1-76`'s direct-over-group precedence; reuse that path or factor it so both callers share it. A snapshot that enumerates differently from the copy path is a snapshot that can show MATCH while the engine copies something else, which is worse than no snapshot.

  ⚠️ CALL IT WITH `includeQuarantined: true`. Its default is `false` -- it filters on `(includeQuarantined || !r.IsQuarantined)` -- and that default is CORRECT for the copy path and WRONG for this one. The copier must not copy to a quarantined follower, so it excludes it. The UI must SHOW a quarantined follower, because the entire value of quarantine to an operator is seeing that a follower has stopped copying and why. A quarantined relationship that silently vanishes from the display is the same defect as config vanishing without an error.

  This is the one place where 'enumerate as the engine acts' and 'show what is configured' genuinely diverge, and the snapshot needs both: the engine's expansion and precedence, with quarantined rows kept in.

B. PER-RELATIONSHIP CONFIG FIELDS. Identity (`Id`, leader, follower), group membership (the group name, or null for a direct relationship), `SizingMode`, the effective ratio, `IsEnabled`, `ArmedForLive`, `IsQuarantined` + `QuarantineReason`, `StealthMode`.

C. EXPECTED POSITION. Compute the expected follower quantity and side from the LEADER'S ACTUAL POSITION by calling `CalculateFollowerQuantity(rel, leaderQty, rawSymbol, currentFollowerPosition, isExit, out isClamped)` -- region R3, the SAME function the copy path calls. Do NOT reimplement the sizing arithmetic in the snapshot; a second copy of that rule is the defect this ticket exists to prevent.

  ⚠️ TWO TRAPS IN THAT CALL. (i) It opens with `if (leaderQty <= 0) return 0;`, so it takes an ABSOLUTE quantity. Passing a signed quantity for a short leader returns 0 and the snapshot silently reports the follower should be flat -- derive the SIDE separately from the leader's `MarketPosition` and pass `Math.Abs(quantity)`. (ii) There is a convenience overload at :812 with a shorter parameter list; call the 6-argument form, because only it exposes `isClamped` and `currentFollowerPosition`.

  Carry `isClamped` on the DTO rather than hiding it -- a clamped expectation is a different statement from an unclamped one, and the operator needs to see which.

D. ACTUAL POSITION. Read the follower's real position the way ReconcileFollowerPosition already does -- `account.Positions.FirstOrDefault(p => p.Instrument == instrument)` (:221-222) -- and carry side + absolute quantity. A null position is FLAT, not an error.

E. VERDICT. One enum per relationship: QUARANTINED, ORPHAN, DIVERGED, SHADOW, MATCH, IDLE.
  - QUARANTINED wins over every position comparison: the relationship is not copying, so agreement is meaningless.
  - ORPHAN = the leader is FLAT and the follower is NOT. It MUST rank above DIVERGED. It is a position on a funded account that nothing is managing, and it is the single worst state this system can report.
  - DIVERGED = both non-flat but the quantity or side disagrees with expected.
  - SHADOW = `IsEnabled` is true and `ArmedForLive` is false. The relationship is configured and will not act.
  - IDLE = leader flat and follower flat. This is a PASS, not a blank -- render it, do not omit it.
  - MATCH = expected equals actual.

F. METRICS MUST CARRY THEIR SAMPLE COUNT. Every metric on the DTO is a pair: the value AND the number of samples behind it. `slippageSamples` comes from `_slippageSampleCounts`. `latencySamples` does not exist yet -- ADD a counter alongside it, keyed the same way by `rel.Id`, and increment it ONLY where a latency is actually recorded. A reading rejected by the sanity bound MUST NOT increment it; that path deliberately does not record a number, and counting it would restore the exact lie this ticket removes. A consumer seeing `latencySamples == 0` must be able to conclude 'never measured' with certainty.

G. THE SNAPSHOT MUST NOT MUTATE ANYTHING. It must NOT call `LoadFromDisk`, must not write config, must not touch `_relationships`, and must not clear or reset a counter. `P1-69` and `P1-75` are both defects where a READ mutated -- one destroyed the in-memory measurements it was asked to report, the other DISARMED the prop-firm rules. A read must not mutate; this is the third chance to get it wrong.

H. IT MUST BE TESTABLE. The new API and its DTOs go OUTSIDE `#if !TESTING`. Reading a position is not order submission; only submission belongs behind that guard.
tickets.context:
⚠️ READ THIS FIRST -- THE SCAFFOLD ALREADY EXISTS. Commit `670cefe` added, in TradeCopierEngine.cs: the enum `CopierConformance`, the classes `CopierMetric`, `CopierSnapshotRow` and `CopierSnapshot`, AND a `GetSnapshot()` method whose body returns an EMPTY snapshot. DO NOT DECLARE ANY OF THESE AGAIN. The first attempt at this ticket failed four rounds on exactly that -- `error CS0101: already contains a definition for 'CopierSnapshot'` and `error CS0111: already defines a member called 'GetSnapshot'` -- because the regions did not include the scaffold and the model reasonably assumed it had to create it. Your job is to REPLACE THE BODY of the existing `GetSnapshot()` (region R1) and to add a latency sample counter (region R2). The DTOs are regions R4/R5/R6: read them, add a field if you genuinely need one, but do not redeclare the types.

⚠️ EXACT MEMBER NAMES -- USE THESE, DO NOT GUESS. The previous attempt failed all four rounds on invented names (`CopierGroup.FollowerAccountNames`, `.LeaderAccountNames`, `.Name`, `.Followers`, `.Leaders`, and `Instrument.Name`). None of those exist.

  `CopierGroup` (region R7): `Id`, `GroupName`, `LeaderAccountName`, `IsEnabled`, `ArmedForLive`, `Mode`, `SizingMode`, `QuantityRatio`, `FixedLotMode`, `FixedLotSize`, `AutoSymbolConversion`, `PerTickerRatios`, `CustomSymbolMappings`, `StealthMode`, `MaxPositionSize`, `DailyLossLimit`, `MaxSlippageTicks`, `FollowerAccounts` (a `List<string>`), and the method `ToRelationships()`.

  `Instrument`: the name is `FullName`. There is NO `.Name` on Instrument -- `Name` lives on `MasterInstrument`, as is `TickSize`. `GetActiveRelationshipsForLeader` returns `CopierRelationship`, whose accounts are `LeaderAccountName` and `FollowerAccountName` (singular, both `string`).

⚠️ A RELATIONSHIP DOES NOT KNOW WHICH GROUP IT CAME FROM. `CopierRelationship` has NO `GroupName` field, and `ToRelationships()` does not add one -- so you cannot read `CopierSnapshotRow.GroupName` off the relationship. Derive it: a row's `GroupName` is the `GroupName` of the group whose `LeaderAccountName` matches the row's leader AND whose `FollowerAccounts` contains the row's follower; `null` when no group matches, which is what makes it a DIRECT relationship. Match account names with `StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase`, as the rest of the engine does.

⚠️ TO ENUMERATE EVERY ROW you need the set of leaders, which is the union of `_relationships`' `LeaderAccountName` and `_groups`' `LeaderAccountName`, de-duplicated case-insensitively. Then call `GetActiveRelationshipsForLeader(leader, includeQuarantined: true)` once per leader.

TradeCopierEngine.cs. `CopierRelationship` is declared at :26 and already carries everything section B needs: `Id`, `LeaderAccountName`, `FollowerAccountName`, `IsEnabled`, `ArmedForLive`, `Mode`, `SizingMode`, `QuantityRatio`, `FixedLotMode`/`FixedLotSize`, `AutoSymbolConversion`, `PerTickerRatios`, `CustomSymbolMappings`, `StealthMode`, `MaxPositionSize`, `DailyLossLimit`, `IsQuarantined`, `QuarantineReason`, `LatencyMs` (:58), `AvgSlippageTicks` (:59) and `MaxSlippageTicks` (:63, a CONFIG THRESHOLD, not a measurement -- do not report it as one).

`GetRelationships()` (:261) returns a defensive copy under `_lock` and is the model for how a read API here behaves. `GetActiveRelationshipsForLeader` (:475) is the one that matters for section A: it merges direct relationships with group-expanded ones and enforces `P1-76` (a follower belongs to a direct relationship OR a group, never both).

`CopierGroup.ToRelationships()` (:87) deep-copies `PerTickerRatios` per follower, so a group-derived relationship is a real relationship, not a view.

The sizing function is region R3. `ReconcileFollowerPosition` is region R2's neighbour and is where the position-read idiom lives (:221-222); its delta math at :191-192 is inside `#if !TESTING` and is the reason no test can reach the comparison today.

`_slippageSampleCounts` is a `Dictionary<string,int>` keyed by `rel.Id`, read and written under `_lock` at :3341-3346. The latency assignment is at :3307. The sanity-bound rejection path logs `(REJECTED by sanity bound, not recorded)` and deliberately leaves `LatencyMs` alone -- that is correct and must stay correct.

MEASURED REALITY, so no test invents a fantasy number: one live 1-lot MNQ round trip produced latency 142.86 ms on the entry and 314.21 ms on the exit, with slippage 0 ticks (a TRUE zero -- both legs filled at 29840.75) and -4 ticks (negative is FAVOURABLE). Milliseconds, not microseconds: these are wall-clock deltas between two NT8 callbacks.

OUT OF SCOPE, do not touch: the config file path (that is UI2), `TradeCopierWindow.cs` in any form (it is excluded from RiskGuardTests.csproj and its future is undecided), any HTTP route, and any change to what the copier submits.
expect_green: snapshot reports IDLE when the leader and the follower are both flat
snapshot reports MATCH when the follower holds the configured multiple of the leader
snapshot reports DIVERGED when the follower quantity is short of the configured multiple
snapshot reports DIVERGED when the follower holds the right quantity on the wrong side
snapshot reports ORPHAN when the leader is flat and the follower is not
snapshot ranks ORPHAN above DIVERGED when both could describe the same row
snapshot reports SHADOW when the relationship is enabled but not armed for live
snapshot reports QUARANTINED in preference to any position comparison
snapshot reports latencySamples 0 and slippageSamples 0 before any fill is observed
snapshot reports latencySamples 1 after one latency is actually recorded
snapshot does not count a latency rejected by the sanity bound as a sample
snapshot counts a slippage sample independently of the latency sample count
snapshot expands a group into one entry per follower account
snapshot reports a follower once when a direct relationship shadows a group membership
snapshot derives expected quantity from the engine's own sizing path rather than a second copy
snapshot carries the clamped flag when the sizing function reports one
snapshot treats a missing follower position as flat rather than as an error
snapshot leaves the engine unmutated and never reloads config from disk

regions.note: THE STUB TO REPLACE. It already exists and already returns an empty snapshot -- replace its BODY, do not add a second method. It already sits below the `#if !TESTING`/`#endif` pair, which is what lets the tests reach it; keep it there. Follow GetRelationships()' lock-and-defensive-copy shape, which is directly above it.

Fill observation, :3244 onward. The latency sample counter is added here, incremented ONLY on the path that actually records a latency (:3307), never on the sanity-bound rejection path. The slippage counter it must sit beside is at :3341-3346.
